methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native represent grassroots peer-to-peer capability building in a non-metro region, exactly the distributed knowledge transfer needed to avoid concentration in NoVA hubs.

signals.title: Griffith Announces $97,472 ARC Grant for AI Study in the Ninth District - Patriot Publishing LLC
signals.signal_reading: A $97K federal grant to study AI in the economically transitioning Ninth District signals exploratory attention but the modest funding scale suggests shallow engagement rather than deep capability development in Appalachian Virginia.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's pediatric AI innovation hub partnership deepens the New River Valley's research capabilities, concentrating advanced AI expertise in an existing academic center rather than distributing it broadly across rural communities.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: An opinion piece explicitly naming data centers as drivers of Virginia's urban-rural divide signals that AI infrastructure investment is concentrating economic benefit in NoVA while bypassing capability-building in other regions.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: AI use strong in Virginia, with Montgomery County at No. 5 statewide - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Montgomery County ranking #5 statewide in AI usage suggests distributed adoption beyond traditional tech hubs, indicating peer networks and community colleges may be enabling broader fluency in smaller Virginia localities.
